items.title: The "One Level Up" Cheat Code for Promotions
items.summary: In episode 1011 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Catherine Williams, Chief Data Officer at Candid her primary guidance for aspiring leaders. She advises thinking about the environment and problems faced by the next level up in the organization, such as a director considering VP-level concerns, to provide valuable solutions and propel one's career.

items.title: Does AI Development Require Advanced Math Expertise?
items.summary:
You don’t always need a cloud API to build something useful with AI.

In this short, Keiji Kamigusa challenges one of the biggest assumptions in AI development: that every serious AI app has to depend on hosted models, API keys, subscriptions, and someone else’s infrastructure.

With local AI, developers can build private chatbots, RAG apps, document tools, voice-enabled assistants, and other real applications directly on a Mac. That means more control, more privacy, fewer external dependencies, and the freedom to experiment without watching every request turn into another line item.

Cloud AI still has its place. But if you want to understand what’s possible on your own machine, Build Applications with Local AI Models on a Mac shows you how to start building.

If you thought “AI app” automatically meant “cloud bill,” this short is for you.

Learn more: https://hubs.la/Q04mY6wQ0

#LocalAI #AIDevelopment #MacAI #AppleSilicon #Ollama #PrivateAI #RAG #AIApps #OnDeviceAI #ManningBooks

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: India's ₹1.6 Lakh Crore Semiconductor Bet Enters Its Next Phase
items.summary:
India's semiconductor journey has moved from policy announcements to commercial production, but the next phase is about building a complete ecosystem.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdeva sits down with Ashok Chandak, President of IESA and SEMI India, to break down how Sanand became India's semiconductor packaging cluster, why Micron, Kaynes Semicon and CG Semi mark a shift from design capability to manufacturing execution, what Semicon 2.0's ₹1.27 lakh crore programme is designed to unlock, and how India can build capabilities in fabs, OSAT, advanced packaging, equipment, materials, talent and chip design. The conversation also examines India's partnership with Japan, Tata Electronics' Dholera fab, the role of fabless startups, semiconductor supply-chain resilience, quantum hardware, and the milestones that could define India's semiconductor success by 2030, including higher domestic value addition, more fabs, OSAT facilities, fabless companies and exports.

items.title: Literally everyone hated this feature
items.summary:
Did Meta actually think we wouldn’t notice this? 🫣

Recently, Meta rolled out a new image-generation feature called Muse Image. On paper, it was pitched as a creative new AI tool. In reality, it turned into a massive privacy and safety concern overnight.

By default, the feature automatically opted in public accounts, allowing anyone to simply @ a handle and use Meta AI to generate entirely new images using that person's likeness with NO permission required.

Unsurprisingly, after immense backlash from users, privacy advocates, and talent agencies, Meta pulled the feature just three days after launch.

But this whole ordeal leaves us with a pretty big question… did Meta genuinely not anticipate this backlash, or was this a calculated move to get eyes on their new AI model?

Let me know which one you think it is in the comments. 👇

#AI #Ainews #genAI
